jsonObj.suggestedValue: Chhath Puja is the most significant festival in Bihar and the Mithila region, dedicated to Surya Dev (the Sun God) and Chhathi Maiya. In Bandwar, the festival is celebrated at the [[bandh|bandh]] along the [[burhi-gandak|Burhi Gandak]], with the entire village gathering on the riverbank. A large idol of Surya Dev, mounted on his chariot with seven horses, is set up at the bandh, and the village observes four days of rigorous fasting and Vedic ritual.

The four-day festival begins with Nahay-Khay, when devotees bathe in river and eat a special meal of rice, chana dal, and kaddu (bottle gourd). The second day is Kharna, when a day-long fast is broken in the evening with roti and kheer. The third day — Sandhya Arghya — is the most important: as the sun sets, devotees stand in the water and offer prayers to the setting sun. The fourth day is Usha Arghya — the same ritual repeated at sunrise, ending the fast. Throughout the four days, devotees observe strict rules of cleanliness and abstinence, and the festival's rituals are considered among the most demanding of any Hindu observance.

The prasad prepared for Chhath is elaborate and strictly vegetarian. It includes thekua (a wheat-and-jaggery biscuit), kheer, fruits (especially sugarcane & banana), and coconut. The prasad is prepared on wood fire in a clean, ritualised manner, and is offered to the sun on bamboo soops (trays). The preparation of thekua is a family activity — women typically gather in the days before the festival to make the biscuits in large batches, and the thekua from different households is exchanged as a gesture of goodwill.
